restored_scope: ItemCreator.ClearCreatedItemsCountExceptPredefined preserves native order: clear real goal prerequisites, clear the SAME generation dictionary, then add the real predefined initial item counts. It neither dequeues nor resets the predefined queue and does not recalculate or reenable set elements.

ItemCreator.UpdateCreatedItemsCountExceptPredefined captures the saved vector length once but resolves the current loader again for each pair, preserves native unchecked replacement arithmetic and duplicate-key behavior, and retains unrelated predefined counts.

The restore loop rereads the live set array, captures each actual set and its element-list identity, reads live element counts, maps tiled/item/goal IDs, looks up limits before saved counts/targets, disables exhausted filling obstacles, updates availability on EACH set, then recalculates the real global fill factors. Required failure and partial mutations are retained.

OriginalLevelSetSelection exposes a cached typed view of its existing ID/availability arrays; captured identity remains stable when FillFourColors grows those arrays. OriginalFillSetGeneration supplies its existing createdCounts dictionary, actual sets, real GoalManager prerequisites/limits, real predefined container and original ratio recalculation.

The decoded saved-count getters require level, board and item-creator values. An absent count vector has length zero; a requested missing vector/pair is a required-value failure. This is a typed projection of already decoded FLevelSaveData, not a replacement for the full binary LevelRestoreManager.

The actual formal first-board composition owns the shared count state without synthetic production restore data. The explicit GameManager entry fixture binds an absent-vector decoded loader and calls that SAME formal owner once during restore. Real session, goal/move values, SQLite attempt persistence, formal population and initial shuffle remain checked.

Unity checks actual clear/predefined dequeue independence, duplicate saved keys, real goal exhaustion and real generation limits, set availability/global ratios, thirty-two subsequent actual fill choices excluding exhausted obstacles, repeated restore without reenabling, captured-list growth and required decoded values. The original classification is preserved: type8 is not a filling obstacle; the integration uses actual type9/tiled26/goal16 for its limit case.

The failed initial Unity fixture and its exact source/log/report are retained. It expected non-filling type8 to be capped; only the fixture was corrected. The runtime classification and count kernel were not changed to satisfy that expectation.

Recorded input regression retains ten accepted swaps, one rejected swap, seventy-six refills, two naturally created specials and twenty moves, with all seventy-two occupied slots and existing no-freeze/landing checks. It is not physical input or visual parity proof.

Actual post-restore selection rejects exhausted obstacles. Full binary save parsing, all concrete item models and production startup/mobile composition remain unverified.

Checks invalid swap spends0, accepted swaps spend1, first triple/three box goals/six refills, 10accepted swaps and naturally observed special creation patterns (each requested type also has its own activation mode), automatic cascades, original creation coroutines and all72 model slots/no holes/no freeze/landing tolerance. remaining_gaps: Production Application/UserContext/account/WinFail/GameManager composition and full112-slot factories are still absent. The fixed first-board gameplay composition remains; an explicit fixture is not a production service.

Full binary saved-level parsing and ownership, complete randomized parsers, all static/initial/filling item models, complete restore-before/after state and runtime shuffle animations/events remain required.

Home/retry/next-level navigation, all level/event/visual/audio branches, country/AB/GM/default-US routing and Android/iOS execution remain unproven. SDK behavior is unchanged and no Android SQLite binary was added.
performance: Clear and restore run only during entry/retry/restore. They share the existing dictionary/arrays and cache one typed element-list adapter per accessed set. No reflection, LINQ, per-frame polling, new resource preload or hierarchy creation is added. Hidden verification reuses the existing independent incremental Unity cache.
